site.name: shopify
site.summary: shopify-clone Clone of the Shopify marketing → trial → admin funnel. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: hero ("Your business starts with Shopify" + email signup input), product features, customer success stories, customer logos, footer | | `pricing.html` | Plan comparison: Basic / Shopify / Advanced three tiers, monthly / yearly toggle, feature comparison table, FAQ | | `free-trial.html` | Trial landing page: 3-step intro to the trial flow, value props restated, large "Start free trial" button |

run_plan.goal: Explore the complete Shopify marketing, pricing, and onboarding funnel to evaluate user experience across form flows, state transitions, and mobile responsiveness.
run_plan.summary: The run will first execute the primary 'Start free trial' onboarding flow, transitioning from the homepage to the multi-step trial form. It will then test the login and account recovery flows on the admin page. Next, it will evaluate the pricing structures and 'Contact Sales' forms. Finally, it will verify informational resources and repeat key interactable checks in the mobile viewport to assess responsive design and tap target sizes.
assumptions: free-trial-form.html contains a client-side multi-step wizard to simulate onboarding.
pricing.html contains a functional monthly/yearly toggle for plan comparisons.
Forms like sales.html and admin.html have basic validation to test.
risk_hotspots: free-trial-form.html multi-step form navigation and state preservation
pricing.html plan comparison table and monthly/yearly toggle usability
sales.html form submission and missing input labels
Small tap targets (below 44px) on navigation links across all pages on mobile

phases.title: Trial Onboarding Flow
phases.objective: Validate the user journey from landing page to completing the onboarding questionnaire.
key_checks: Email input submission on index.html routing to trial flow
Navigation through the multi-step questionnaire in free-trial-form.html using 'Next'
Functionality of the 'Skip all' button during onboarding
Final success state or redirect upon finishing the questionnaire
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated through all steps of free-trial-form.html to the final state.

phases.title: Authentication & Admin
phases.objective: Test the login interface and recovery paths for existing merchants.
key_checks: Validation of email, password, and store URL inputs
Functionality of 'Log in' button and success/error states
Presence and responsiveness of 'Forgot password?' link
Clickability of social login options (Apple, Google, Facebook)
exit_criteria: Login form interacted with and error/success states observed.

phases.title: Pricing and Enterprise Sales
phases.objective: Evaluate the plan comparison features and lead generation forms.
key_checks: Toggling between 'Pay monthly' and 'Pay yearly' on pricing.html
Filling out the Contact Sales form on sales.html
Validating dropdown selects (company size, topic) on sales.html
exit_criteria: Pricing toggle changes state and Sales form can be submitted.

phases.title: Resources and Help Center
phases.objective: Ensure support and marketing content is accessible and well-structured.
key_checks: Navigation links in resources.html point to correct sections
Help center search input functionality in help-trial.html
Readability and layout of help center articles
exit_criteria: Resource links and help center search interacted with.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Verify that critical paths and dense layouts are usable on smaller screens.
key_checks: Tap target sizes for navigation and form buttons
Responsiveness of the pricing table and multi-step onboarding form
exit_criteria: Key pages checked in mobile viewport with layout warnings documented.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise form flows (onboarding, login, sales) and state toggles (pricing).
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the primary free trial onboarding and pricing checks in mobile viewport to evaluate responsive layout.

notes: Pay special attention to the layout warnings regarding small tap targets, as they are prevalent across multiple pages and could be a major UX issue on mobile.

Shopify is a complete commerce platform that lets you start, grow, and manage a business. If you use Shopify Payments, there are no additional transaction fees. observation.title: Trying Shopify with a free trial – Shopify Help Center
observation.visible_text: Shopify Help Center ON THIS PAGE Available plans for trial Initiate the free trial Setting up your store Making the most of your trial Choosing a paid plan Trial period length Promotional pricing Deactivating your store Troubleshooting Trying Shopify with a free trial To explore Shopify before committing to an active monthly plan, you can sign up for a free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. The new plan takes effect immediately, but you aren't charged until your free trial period ends. Free trial period length and details The length of your free trial can vary based on different factors. To find out the current trial length and any promotional offers available, visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. observation.title: Trying Shopify with a free trial – Shopify Help Center
observation.visible_text: Shopify Help Center ON THIS PAGE Available plans for trial Initiate the free trial Setting up your store Making the most of your trial Choosing a paid plan Trial period length Promotional pricing Deactivating your store Troubleshooting Trying Shopify with a free trial To explore Shopify before committing to an active monthly plan, you can sign up for a free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. The new plan takes effect immediately, but you aren't charged until your free trial period ends. Free trial period length and details The length of your free trial can vary based on different factors. To find out the current trial length and any promotional offers available, visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Note: It's not possible to extend the duration of your free trial period. If you decide to upgrade to a paid plan within your free trial period, then charges wi

observation.title: Trying Shopify with a free trial – Shopify Help Center
observation.visible_text: Shopify Help Center ON THIS PAGE Available plans for trial Initiate the free trial Setting up your store Making the most of your trial Choosing a paid plan Trial period length Promotional pricing Deactivating your store Troubleshooting Trying Shopify with a free trial To explore Shopify before committing to an active monthly plan, you can sign up for a free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. The new plan takes effect immediately, but you aren't charged until your free trial period ends. Free trial period length and details The length of your free trial can vary based on different factors. To find out the current trial length and any promotional offers available, visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Note: It's not possible to extend the duration of your free trial period. If you decide to upgrade to a paid plan within your free trial period, then charges wi

observation.title: Start Your Free Trial – Shopify
observation.visible_text: Shopify Log in Start free trial Your business starts with Shopify Start for free, keep building for £1/month. Plus, earn up to £7,000 in credits as you sell. Start free trial You agree to receive Shopify marketing emails. Allbirds Gymshark Brooklinen Leesa Kylie Cosmetics Crate & Barrel Monos CUSTOMIZABLE THEMES Create a stunning store in seconds Pre-built designs make it fast and easy to kickstart your brand. Total sales £700,000 +£7,000 GET REWARDED Your plan can pay for itself Turn sales into savings with 1% back as subscription credits. MEET SIDEKICK Level up with our AI assistant With millions of AI tokens to use with our built-in assistant, you can grow without limits. Hey Arda, How can I help? Ask Sidekick anything about your store... Shop Pay Klarna Mastercard Visa ALL-IN-ONE Getting stuff done? Done. Shopify handles everything from secure payments to marketing and hardware. "We've tripled in size since we first started on Shopify. It gives us the tools we need to keep pushing forward." — Shopify Merchant No risk, all rewards. Try Shopify for £1/month. Plus, earn up to £7,000 in credits as you sell. Start free trial You agree to receive Shopify marketing emails. Questions? What is Shopify and how does it work? Shopify is a complete commerce platform that lets you start, grow, and manage a business. With Shopify, you can build an online store, manage sales, market to customers, and accept payments in digital and physical locations. How much does Shopify cost? Try Shopify free for 3 days, no credit card required. After your trial expires, choose a pricing plan that suits the size and stage of your business. Can I use my own domain name with Shopify? Yes, you can use your own domain name with Shopify. If you have an existing domain name, you can connect it to Shopify from your store's admin. If you don't have a domain name yet, you can either buy one through Shopify or a third-party provider. Do I need to be a designer or developer to use Shopify? No, you don't need to be a designer or developer to use Shopify. Signing up for Shopify allows you to use pre-built themes, drag-and-drop editors, and AI tools to create your store without any coding knowledge.
